faq.q: Why do fake stories spread faster?
faq.a: False stories are often more surprising and emotional than real news, so people share them quickly. The MIT study found people, not robots, did most of that spreading.
asks: Why is fake news so viral?

faq.a: An algorithm is a set of step-by-step rules a computer follows. Social media algorithms choose which posts you see, often favouring ones that get lots of likes, comments and shares.
asks: How do apps choose what I see?

faq.q: Why do we believe things we see often?
faq.a: Our brains find familiar ideas easier to process, and that ease feels like truth. Psychologists call this the illusory truth effect.
asks: What is the illusory truth effect?

faq.q: What is the difference between misinformation and disinformation?
faq.a: Misinformation is false information shared by mistake. Disinformation is false information spread on purpose, to trick people, make money or push a political goal.
asks: Who makes fake news and why?

faq.q: How can I stop fake news spreading?
faq.a: Pause before sharing, check the source and other reports, and do not comment on or share posts you think are false, because that boosts them. Gently share a correction instead.
asks: What can I do about fake news?

facts: A 2018 MIT study in Science found false news on Twitter was about 70% more likely to be retweeted than true news.
Misinformation is false information shared by mistake; disinformation is false information spread on purpose.

quiz.say: What does a social media algorithm do?
quiz.show: What does a social media algorithm do?
quiz.why: It follows rules to decide which posts appear in your feed.

wrong.0: Reporters and users write posts; the algorithm sorts them.
wrong.1: Cameras take photos; algorithms rank and show them.

quiz.say: Where can you best break the fake news loop?
quiz.show: Where can you best break the fake news loop?
quiz.why: If you pause and check before sharing, the story stops with you.

wrong.1: By then millions may have seen it; it is much harder to stop.
wrong.2: Each person who checks before sharing slows the loop down.
